extract:
The Smashing Pumpkins formed in Chicago in 1988. They emerged from the city's club circuit alongside the alternative rock boom that would soon break nationally. Singer, guitarist and principal songwriter Billy Corgan started the band with guitarist James Iha, adding bassist D'arcy Wretzky and jazz-trained drummer Jimmy Chamberlin. Corgan's tastes drew on 1970s hard rock and psychedelia, goth, and British shoegaze, a mix that set the group apart from the punk-rooted grunge of Seattle. Early singles included "I Am One" on the local label Limited Potential and "Tristessa" on Sub Pop.

Their debut album, Gish (1991), was released on Caroline Records and produced by Butch Vig shortly before he recorded Nirvana's Nevermind. It paired heavy, phased guitars with dreamy passages and became a strong independent seller. The band moved to Virgin Records for Siamese Dream (1993), again with Vig. The sessions were famously fraught, with Corgan playing many of the guitar and bass parts himself. The album's layered wall of overdubbed guitars on "Cherub Rock," "Today" and "Disarm" made it a multi-platinum breakthrough. In 1994 they headlined Lollapalooza and released Pisces Iscariot, a compilation of B-sides and outtakes.

Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness (1995) was an ambitious double album co-produced by Flood and Alan Moulder. It ranged from the metallic "Bullet with Butterfly Wings" and "Zero" to the orchestral "Tonight, Tonight" and the drum-machine-tinged "1979," and it became one of the best-selling double albums of the decade. "Bullet with Butterfly Wings" won a Grammy for Best Hard Rock Performance, and the band later won another for "The End Is the Beginning Is the End" from the Batman & Robin soundtrack. In 1996 touring keyboardist Jonathan Melvoin died of an overdose, and Chamberlin was dismissed from the band. Without him, the group made Adore (1998), a subdued, electronic and acoustic record that sold well below its predecessors.

Chamberlin returned for Machina/The Machines of God (2000), but Wretzky had departed and was replaced by Melissa Auf der Maur, formerly of Hole. After clashing with Virgin, the band distributed a companion album, Machina II, for free online, then broke up at the end of 2000. Corgan went on to form Zwan. He and Chamberlin revived the Smashing Pumpkins name in the mid-2000s and released Zeitgeist in 2007. Corgan then led the band with rotating lineups, including on Oceania (2012) and Monuments to an Elegy (2014), the latter featuring Mötley Crüe's Tommy Lee on drums.

Critics have long ranked Siamese Dream and Mellon Collie among the defining records of 1990s alternative rock. The band's blend of metal heft, shoegaze texture and arena-scale melodrama distinguished them from contemporaries such as Nirvana, Pearl Jam and Soundgarden. Corgan's outsized ambition and public feuds became part of the band's story as much as the music. Their influence can be heard in later alternative, emo and heavy shoegaze acts.

In 2018 Iha rejoined Corgan and Chamberlin for a reunion tour and the Rick Rubin-produced Shiny and Oh So Bright, Vol. 1 / LP: No Past. No Future. No Sun. Since then the band has continued to tour and record, releasing the synth-heavy Cyr (2020) and the sprawling rock opera Atum, a sequel to Mellon Collie and Machina. They remain one of the most commercially successful and stylistically restless bands of their generation.
title: The Smashing Pumpkins
